- hyperframes: Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.
- hyperframes-animation: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.
- hyperframes-audio: Use when audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition needs to be mixed: fade-in/fade-out, crossfade, track gain or volume, volume automation, ducking, a music bed that fights a voiceover (voiceover carve), effects on a track (EQ, compressor, limiter, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, chorus, phaser, bitcrush), or automation envelopes drawn on a track's volume or any effect parameter. Don't use for sourcing or generating audio — finding BGM, SFX, or making a voiceover is `/media-use`. Don't use for clip timing or track layout, which is `/hyperframes-core`.
- hyperframes-cli: Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.
- hyperframes-core: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Also covers Tailwind projects and the STORYBOARD.md / SCRIPT.md plan formats. Read before writing composition HTML.
- hyperframes-creative: Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`.
- hyperframes-keyframes: Use when a HyperFrames composition needs a punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns treatment, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; also for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.
- hyperframes-registry: Install, discover, and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR).
- media-use: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal.
- motion-graphics: A short, design-led motion graphic where motion is the message — kinetic typography, stat count-up, chart/data-viz hit, logo sting / brand lockup, lower-third / callout / social overlay, animated map (highlight regions, connect places, zoom to a location), animated tweet / news-article / headline, webpage / UI animation (scroll, cursor, callouts), or fusing a real image's geometry into a chart. Usually under 10s (up to ~30s), no narration or live-action subject; renders to MP4 or transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / multi-scene → /general-video. Unclear → /hyperframes.

NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)

4	(`app/projects/[id]/**`). Marketing pages (`app/page.tsx`, `/pricing`, `/blog`,

7	## The one-sentence brief
8	
9	An AI website builder that happens to have a customer portal around it — not a
10	dashboard that happens to contain a builder. The primary action is always
11	"build something".
12

18	Tailwind class, never a raw hex and never an arbitrary-value bracket.**

25	| `bg-surface` | Cards, panels, the sidebar. |

83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`.
101	
102	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
103	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
108	
109	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
110	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
111	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
112	
113	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
114	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
115	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
116	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
117	and not a progress bar.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
122	
123	| Thing | Reality |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
126	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
127	| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
128	| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
129	| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
130	| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
131	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
132	| **Support tickets** | No ticket model. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and explicitly never shown to the customer. |
133	| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
134	| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
135	| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |
136	
137	**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, are now BUILT** — see
138	`/settings/security` and `/settings`. Note what `Session` actually records:
139	`id · userId · tokenHash · expiresAt · createdAt`, and nothing else. There is no
140	user agent, no IP, no last-seen and no device. Do not add a column for them
141	casually: `/legal/rights` and the data export both enumerate in writing
142	everything the database holds, so a new personal-data field silently makes two
143	published documents wrong.
144	
145	### The rule
146	
147	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
148	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
149	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.

 * and the wedding page for two first names — and why no template is asked
 * anything its prompt would not use.

 *   - ROW REPEATS. `[date] / [venue] / [city]` in the band's gig list, `[time]

/** Never throws for an unknown id — an unmapped template simply asks nothing
    and starts from its prompt as written, which is a valid outcome. */
export function fieldsFor(templateId: string): IntakeField[] {
  return TEMPLATE_FIELDS[templateId] ?? [];
}

const MAX_TEXT = 120;
const MAX_LONG = 260;

/**
 * What actually goes into the prompt.
 *
 * Square brackets are stripped from the answer: the prompt's whole convention
 * is that a bracket means "this is still unknown", and letting someone type
 * `[TBD]` into a field would quietly hand the builder a placeholder that looks
 * like an instruction. Newlines collapse because every one of these tokens sits
 * inline in a sentence.
 */
export function cleanAnswer(raw: string, kind: IntakeField["kind"]): string {
  return raw
    .replace(/[[\]]/g, "")
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .trim()
    .slice(0, kind === "long" ? MAX_LONG : MAX_TEXT)
    .trim();
}

/**
 * The palette block, in the vocabulary `lib/wizard.ts` already established: the
 * preset id, the literal stops and an instruction to pull the real source
 * through `find_assets` rather than improvising a lookalike. No adjective ever
 * travels on its own.
 */
function paletteBlock(choice: PaletteChoice): string {
  const p = choice.palette;
  return [
    "Visual direction — I chose these colours, so build to them rather than picking your own. Where this disagrees with a colour hint earlier in the brief, this wins:",
    `- Palette: ${choice.id} (${choice.colors.join(" to ")}). Use find_assets with the query "${choice.id}" to pull the exact gradient source, make those the dominant colours, and derive the rest from those hexes. Do not substitute a different colour.`,
    `- Primary ${p.primary}, secondary ${p.secondary}, accent ${p.accent}.`,
    `- Page: ${p.ink} text on ${p.surface}. Keep the dark mode working.`,
  ].join("\n");
}

const LOGO_BLOCK = [
  "My logo is attached to this build as a reference image.",
  "Recreate it as inline SVG or as a simple type lockup in the header and the footer — do not link to a file, and do not leave an empty logo box. Take the palette's lead from it where that does not fight the direction above.",
].join(" ");

/**
 * Template prompt + answers + choices, as one editable string.
 *
 * Pure and deterministic: the same inputs always produce the same text, which
 * is what lets the review step re-derive the prompt after an edit is reverted
 * and what makes "go back, change one answer, come forward" show a diff the
 * customer can actually follow.
 */
export function assembleTemplatePrompt({
  template,
  answers,
  palette,
  hasLogo,
}: {
  template: Template;
  answers: Record<string, string>;
  palette: PaletteChoice | null;
  hasLogo: boolean;
}): string {
  let body = template.prompt;

  for (const field of fieldsFor(template.id)) {
    const value = cleanAnswer(answers[field.id] ?? "", field.kind);
    if (!value) continue;
    for (const token of field.tokens) body = body.split(token).join(value);
  }

  return [body.trim(), palette ? paletteBlock(palette) : "", hasLogo ? LOGO_BLOCK : ""]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join("\n\n");
}

/** True once anything has been typed or chosen — drives the "you have unsaved
    answers" affordances rather than a naive dirty flag on every keystroke. */
export function hasIntake(answers: Record<string, string>): boolean {
  return Object.values(answers).some((v) => v.trim() !== "");
}

content.text: Everything typechecks and lints clean. Here's the summary. ## Files (all new, all under `components/templates/`) - `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\templates\TemplatePickerModal.tsx` — the stub replaced; exact signature preserved - `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\templates\TemplateCover.tsx` — cover generation - `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\templates\intake.ts` — per-template questions + prompt assembly - `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\templates\PalettePicker.tsx` - `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\templates\logo.ts` Nothing in `app/**`, `lib/**`, `components/ui/**`, `components/wizard/**`, `TemplateCard.tsx` or `TemplateGallery.tsx` was touched. ## Cover generation **The cover is a miniature abstract wireframe of the page that template builds**, painted in that template's own palette. Not a screenshot, not a photo, no `` — bars, tiles and rules. A restaurant is a hero band over a two-column priced menu with leader dots; a photographer is a masonry grid of mixed-aspect tiles; a tradesperson is one enormous call button; a band is a record sleeve plus tracklist; a blog is a single narrow reading measure. Four independent axes, all from `lib/assets`: 1. **23 layout archetypes**, one per template — distinct before any colour is applied. 2. **23 distinct `GRADIENTS` presets** run through `paletteFromPreset()`, so each mini-page gets the brand kit's own contrast-checked ink/surface pair. The dark presets (ink → barbershop, midnight → product launch, plum-night → band) yield a dark mini-page, which is itself a signal. 3. **A `PATTERNS` texture** over the gradient: barber stripes on the barbershop, checkerboard on the food truck, ruled lines on the blog, blueprint grid on the trades page. 4. **23 different `ICONS` glyphs** in the hero, over a `BACKDROPS` generator seeded by the template id. Deterministic: literal recipe, seed = template id, no clock and no `Math.random`. Covers are resolved once per id and cached. **Verified by rendering all 23**: I transpiled the component, rendered it with `react-dom/server`, served it, and measured in a real browser (screenshots were unavailable — the browser pane wouldn't composite). All 23 gradients distinct, every backdrop and icon group actually present in the DOM, zero `NaN`/`undefined` coordinates, nothing out of bounds. Pairwise raster comparison caught two problems I then fixed: `accountancy` and `coffee-shop` had converged on the same "list left, panel right" shape (accountancy rebuilt as a two-column checked list over a fee strip), and `coffee-shop`'s terracotta sat next to `restaurant`'s ember in the gallery as two adjacent warm oranges (moved to `butter`, whose catalogue keywords are literally "cafe bakery light"). Also added a drop under the page card and a hairline on the hero's bottom edge, because the palest presets (butter, blush, lavender, paper) otherwise put a white page on an almost-white gradient with no visible edge. Raw hex is used only for that artwork — catalogue data, same as `LookPicker` — and each cover is a self-contained tile that renders identically in both themes rather than inheriting either. No text ever sits on it; the covers are `aria-hidden` since the card heading carries the meaning. ## Per-template questions Derived from each prompt's own bracketed placeholders — those brackets already *are* the question list, written by whoever wrote the prompt. Each field declares the literal token it replaces. **133 tokens across 23 templates, all verified by script to exist verbatim in their prompt.** So the restaurant is asked for cuisine, city, address, hours; the photographer for speciality, region and the occasion clients are planning; the accountant for its pricing basis and software. Three kinds of bracket are deliberately *not* asked about, and stay as placeholders: row repeats (the band's `[date]/[venue]/[city]` gig list, the conference's `[time]/[session title]/[speaker name]`, the agency's three `[client name]`s — one answer can't fill a list), examples (`[photo: ceremony, Ravenswood barn]` is showing the model a caption shape), and policy prose (`[your cancellation policy]`, gift wording — these are paragraphs, and the editable prompt box is the honest place for them). Hard cases: **consultant** names its discipline twice in two differently-worded brackets — one question, two tokens. **Wedding** needs two separate name fields; a single combined answer leaves a stray second bracket in the hero, which is the known rough edge in `lib/wizard.ts`'s generic substitution. **link-in-bio** has eight link placeholders; asking for all eight is a wall, so three are asked and the rest stay bracketed (stated in the field hint). ## What is optional Everything in stage 2. Every field, the logo, the palette. Skipping leaves the bracket in place, which is exactly what all 23 prompts instruct the builder to do with a fact it hasn't been given — so the degraded case is the hand-written prompt, unchanged, which already works. Nothing is required or validated. The assembled prompt is shown in an editable textarea before committing, with "Undo my edits" when a hand-edit has diverged. Answers, logo, palette and edits are held per template id, so Back → forward loses nothing, and closing doesn't clear them. Logo: PNG/JPEG/WebP only, downscaled in-browser to `LOGO_LIMITS.RASTER_MAX_EDGE` (160px, the repo's own logo constant). PNG first so transparency survives — JPEG on a transparent logo paints it black — falling back to white-flattened JPEG only if the PNG misses the 16 KiB cap, and refusing with a stated reason if it still does. Output always matches the generate route's `data:image/(png|jpeg|webp);base64,` regex. Palette uses `paletteCatalogue()` — the same presets, ids and hexes `LookPicker` already shows — and the prompt block mirrors `lib/wizard.ts`'s wording (preset id + literal stops + "pull the exact source via find_assets"), so no adjective travels alone. Result returns `[primary, secondary, accent]`. Accessibility: `Modal`'s native `` gives the focus trap, inert background and Escape; on top of that the `h2` retitles per stage, sections are `h3`, focus moves into the intake panel going forward and back onto the card you came from returning, and a `role="status"` line announces the change. `k-focus` on every interactive element except `SearchInput`, where `className` lands on the wrapper and the input already carries `Field.tsx`'s shared control ring (noted in a comment). ## Untested - **No pixel screenshot** of the covers or the modal — the browser pane wouldn't composite in this session. Verification was DOM/geometry/raster measurement in a real browser plus a static React render, not a human look. The covers are worth an eyeball before shipping, particularly the six pale ones (butter, blush, lavender, paper, stone, candy). - The modal was **never mounted** — no page imports it yet, so the open/close lifecycle, focus moves and the `` interaction are reasoned-about, not exercised. - `prepareLogo` was not run against a real file; the PNG→JPEG fallback path in particular is untested. - Covers are drawn on a 320×180 canvas with `slice`; at the list view's 64×40 they will crop noticeably. Intended, but unseen.
